procedure: Sourced ESP-IDF v5.5.4 from /Users/vincenzo/esp/esp-idf-v5.5.4/export.sh so pyserial was available.
Ran python3 scripts/manual_review_display.py button-approve --port /dev/cu.usbmodem1101 --request-id manual-button-approve-2026-05-09 from nSealr/esp32 revision d455056.
The script sent one valid disabled sign_event review request and verified the expected serial response.
The human operator confirmed the display started on Event / Page 1/4.
The human operator pressed short KEY/GPIO14 three times to reach the final page, then long KEY/GPIO14 to approve.
The human operator confirmed the final frame matched Review OK / Closed / Not signed / Signing disabled.
expected_result: The manual button-approve scenario shows a valid review request, allows physical page traversal and approve closure, and still keeps real signing disabled.
observed_result: The script passed with 1 verified serial exchange and 1 response frame. Manual physical confirmation matched the printed checklist: Event / Page 1/4 appeared first, short KEY/GPIO14 page traversal reached the final page, long KEY/GPIO14 closed the review, and the final display showed Review OK / Closed / Not signed / Signing disabled. sign_event remained signing_disabled.
limitations: This is manual display and physical-control acceptance evidence only; it is not production signing acceptance.
Approve closes the RAM-only review session but does not authorize or execute signing.
The protocol response for sign_event remains signing_disabled.
No persistent key custody, secure boot, flash encryption, debug-lock, enclosure, or production approval policy was validated.
